Question B-001-016-010.

Why the correct answer is right: Fast-scan television on 14.23 MHz is prohibited because 14.23 MHz is in the between-7-and-25-MHz group with a 6 kHz limit, and fast-scan ATV occupies more bandwidth than that limit allows.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Slow-scan television (SSTV) on 14.23 MHz": SSTV on 14.23 MHz can fit the 6 kHz group; fast-scan ATV cannot fit that HF bandwidth limit.
- sourceIndex 2: "Frequency modulation (FM) on 29.60 MHz": At 29.60 MHz, the signal is in the 10-metre bandwidth category; a 5 kHz-deviation FM signal is taught as occupying between 10 kHz and 20 kHz, so this choice fits that limit.
- sourceIndex 3: "Single sideband (SSB) on 3.76 MHz": 3.76 MHz is inside the 80-metre band, and ordinary SSB voice is about 2 kHz to 3 kHz wide rather than a fast-scan-video-width signal.
